Ithiel and Ucal were perhaps pupils.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7947"/><div sID="gen12289" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7947"/>24-31. These verses provide two classes of apt illustrations of various aspects of the moral world, which the reader is left to apply. By the first (<reference osisRef="Prov.30.25-Prov.30.28">Pr 30:25-28</reference>), diligence and providence are commended; the success of these insignificant animals being due to their instinctive sagacity and activity, rather than strength. The other class (<reference osisRef="Prov.30.30">Pr 30:30</reference>, <reference osisRef="Prov.30.31">31</reference>) provides similes for whatever is majestic or comely, uniting efficiency with gracefulness. <div eID="gen12289" type="x-p"/>
